answer: A random 19% of submissions is pulled for manual review, and a reviewer's finding of fabrication voids the answer and starts a probation. Because the whisper sample is drawn from the terrace beacon, the grove audit exposes the selection was not made by the operator, and the probation is recorded per key. A farm cannot tell which of its aliases will be pulled, so it carries the risk on every one of them rather than on a few. That is 12 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
